## Welcome to the Mini Project Portal

This platform serves as the central hub for the **20MAD481/482 Mini Project**. Here, you will find the official syllabus mandates, evaluation rubrics, computational project themes, and the standardized formatting templates required for your final submissions.

### Course Objective
The goal of this course is to bridge the gap between abstract mathematical theory and applied computer science. You will move beyond utilizing "black-box" libraries to computationally model, optimize, and simulate complex systems using linear algebra, calculus, and discrete mathematics.

---

### Quick Links & Next Steps

If you are just starting the semester, please follow these steps in order:

1. **[Review the Evaluation Rubric](syllabus.qmd):** Understand exactly how the 150 marks are distributed across the Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) and the End Semester Examination (ESE).
2. **[Read the Implementation Guidelines](guidelines.qmd):** Review the strict 14-week Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) and understand the requirements for your weekly logbook sign-offs.
3. **[Select a Project Theme](projects.qmd):** Browse the 12 curated computational analytics and machine learning themes.
4. **Download the LaTeX Template:** Access the official department template for your final report drafting.
   * [Download `template.tex`](assets/latex/template.tex)
